title: Settlement payouts, STK fixes, and clearer client status
items: Settlement payout method: choose phone number, till/paybill, or bank (dropdown, paybill, account number) — not phone-only.
Fixed staff-initiated STK push failing with "invalid phone number" or "gateway not configured" for platform-collected tenants.
SMS broadcasts, bulk messages, and outage alerts now send once per customer, not once per PPPoE line.
Clients list: Plan/Router/Expiry moved under each account's Services tab; Status now shows Online, last seen, or Blocked.
Payout failures are now logged server-side instead of only showing in the browser.

title: Fixed the settlement payout method dropdown showing blank
items: Settings → Payment gateways: the payout method and bank dropdowns now actually list their options.

title: Clients list rearranged: A/C no, name, wallet, email, service, phone, registered, status
items: Columns reordered to A/C No, Client name, Wallet, Email, Service, Phone, Registered, Status.
Row actions are now a single "Actions ▾" dropdown: View, Services, Edit client, Delete client.

title: Expenses with suppliers, monthly bills and profit & loss; clearer client status
items: Expenses: monthly bills that add themselves to the log before they are due, suppliers with payment details, and paid payroll recorded automatically.
New Profit & loss tab: PPPoE and hotspot income against paid expenses, month by month.
Clients: the package name, a coloured online/offline dot and days left. Clients blocked for 4 months become dormant, and are deleted after 5.
Settings → Message templates, staff ID badges with expiry, and staff password reset.

title: Licence & billing: pay by M-Pesa prompt or paybill; payouts in full on your schedule
items: New Licence & billing page: see what is owed, pay with an M-Pesa prompt to your own phone, or pay to the paybill with your reference.
If a licence expires, only the dashboard becomes view-only — customers and hotspot visitors are never affected.
Payouts are paid in full (no commission deducted), daily, weekly or manual — choose under Settings → Gateways.
Platform fees are billed monthly instead: 3% of hotspot sales plus KES 16 per active PPPoE client.
The free trial is 14 days and is never invoiced.
An expired licence now opens a dedicated page with the ways to pay. Payouts pause until it is renewed and are released afterwards.
After the 14-day free trial, KES 500 activates your licence for 30 days — pay by M-Pesa prompt or paybill.
An expired licence now locks the dashboard completely — only the licence and payment page opens. Customers and hotspot visitors are never affected.
Tenants who host for themselves can be billed a flat monthly fee, and their server shows the licence-expired page if it lapses.

title: Invoice links, SaaS revenue overview, smarter leads
items: SaaS revenue: recurring revenue, collection rate, churn, next-month forecast and who owes what.
Tenants can be billed by revenue share or a flat tier; licence days are added on top of what is left, and spare credit turns into licence months.
Payout & pay-in history now shows SMS credit sales and each tenant's collected, settled and remaining balance.
Invoices: download a PDF, and share a link a customer can open and pay from with an M-Pesa prompt — no login needed.
Leads: filter by stage, installer and channel; assign an installer to many at once; add the package they asked about; see why leads are lost; new Insights tab.
A lead's referrer (the channel) earns the commission and the sales credit; "Installer" is the technician who follows up the installation.
Staff: a Reset password button that sends the new password by SMS and email.
Popups, toasts and update notices now open on the screen in dark mode instead of far down the page.
Payment gateways: the platform paybill can now be saved even when the owner's own ISP portal uses the same paybill number.
Site payment profiles: choose per site whether customers pay through the platform (settled to you) or your own paybill, so one ISP can use both.
Tickets: the list now shows the client on every ticket (name, account and location), and marks installations.
Leads: a won lead has a Raise installation ticket button, and adding the client from a won lead goes straight to the ticket with the client and installer already chosen.
Referral commission is now a percentage of the service package the client signed up for, not of the money their first payment happened to be.
Installation fee: set a standard fee under Settings → Preferences; adding a client charges it as an invoice, and you can change it or waive it for any one client.

Declaring a lead won now raises the installation ticket automatically (assigned to the lead's installer, with who to call and what they bought); adding the client from the lead attaches them to that ticket.
Sales leaderboard now counts the service package fee only — installation fees, top-ups and months paid ahead no longer inflate a salesperson's figure (Leads → Performance and Employee of the Month).
Payments → All transactions shows the voucher code issued for hotspot (KopoKopo) payments, and the phone number the prompt was sent to.
Licence & billing: the amount box is pre-filled with what you owe, or, when nothing is invoiced yet, what this month's statement stands at so far.
Monthly tenant statements are now raised on the last day of the month (23:55), instead of the 1st of the next month.
Each monthly statement now shows when it is due: by default the 5th of the next month at 10:00 AM (Licence & billing → Pay by).
No more free trial: a new tenant is free until the 5th of the next month at 10:00 AM (sign up on the 1st: about five weeks; on the 21st: about two), then pays each month by the 5th.
A statement unpaid by its due time (the 5th, 10:00 AM) now locks the licence until it is paid.
The licence counter in the top bar counts down to the exact lock time (days and hours, then hours and minutes).
A named TV, console or device keeps its reserved IP for a week after its plan expires, so it reconnects on the same address when it pays again; the IP is given back after 7 days.
Fixed expiry reminders, one-off SMS and bulk SMS naming the tenant's own paybill for customers on a router set to collect through the platform; the {paybill} tag now follows the customer's router.
Site payment profiles can now be viewed and edited, not just added or deleted.
A client with a due, unpaid invoice now shows a negative balance (-KES) in the client list and on their account.

Clients table: a new Invoices action, and each client's Invoices page, let you create, view, edit and delete invoices. New invoices are itemised (description, quantity, price) with quick-add lines for installation, package, router and reconnection, payment terms (due now, 3, 7, 14, 30 days or a date) and the tax worked out in the total.
When a client pays, what they already owe (installation fee and other due invoices) is cleared first, oldest first; only the rest buys service or goes to the wallet.
Hotspot plans: a name like "2 devices" must match the Devices field, and changing a plan's device count now updates the routers and the codes already sold, so a second device can connect.
Client → Live data now shows how long the customer has been online this session and how much they have downloaded and uploaded in that time.
Routers → System info shows the data the router has carried since it last started, and each client's PPPoE service shows how long it has been online and the data used in that session.

New: the field technician app (Field app in the menu, also installable on a phone): jobs, closing photos, customer look-up with their PPPoE login, shifts with an accurate location, equipment with serial photos and stock deduction, raising tickets and leads from the phone, working with no signal. Turn it on per role with "Use the technician app".
New: Field team shows where technicians are while they are on shift. Tickets have a job type (repair or install), and a ticket's photos and equipment show on it.
Leads: a lead logged from the field shows its pinned location with a View on map link.

Online but no internet: every 10 minutes the system checks online PPPoE lines; one that is connected, moving nothing and not answering a ping is flagged "Online · not answering" in the clients list (and has its own filter).
Client → Live data has a Diagnose button that checks the account, the router session, the router's own internet, the customer's device and the traffic, and says the likely cause in plain words.
Fixed: the online time and data used for a PPPoE service now show on the Services tab and the Live data tab (they were not being displayed). They are read straight from the router.
A Troubleshoot button on each PPPoE service (client → Services) and in the clients table menu: asks the router what is wrong with a line that is online but has no internet and says the likely cause.

Client → Statistics shows the exact data used each day, grouped by month for the last 12 months; click a month to see every day of it. Counting starts from this update, earlier figures are approximate.
Client → Communication now lists every SMS and email the customer has received, including the automatic ones (receipts, reminders, expiry notices), not just messages typed on the Messaging screen.

Settings → Organisation: choose the country (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, Zambia, South Africa and more) and the currency. Customers' phone numbers are now read and texted in that country's format instead of always as Kenyan numbers.

New payment methods outside Kenya: Flutterwave (Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ghana, Zambia, Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal), Paystack (Ghana, Nigeria, South Africa), AzamPay (Tanzania) and Yo! Payments (Uganda). Add them under Settings → Payment gateways, pick one for the hotspot under Hotspot → Settings, and click Webhook URL to see what to paste into the provider's dashboard.
Hotspot pages show prices in the tenant's own currency, and a payment link when the provider needs one.
A cookie notice appears the first time someone opens the site: Accept all or Essential only, remembered for a year, and changeable from Cookie settings in the footer.

Dashboard → Top commission earner: "sales closed" now counts the clients whose first payment earned the commission, instead of showing 0 when the lead was never marked won. Adding a client from a lead now marks that lead won.
Leads: once a won lead's installation ticket is resolved, the Install ticket button becomes "✓ Installed" instead of staying as a call to raise it again.

New: Schedule. Book installations and repairs for a date, time and technician on a weekly calendar (or from a ticket's Schedule a visit button). The customer is texted the booking and a reminder a few hours before, the technician is texted where to go, double-booking a technician is flagged, and booked jobs show their time in the field app.

Payments → By site: pick the dates (today, yesterday, 7 or 30 days, this or last month, or your own), see each day's takings split by site, and every applied payment is now counted once so the totals match All transactions. Payments with no site are under Unassigned.
vibelink.tech home page redesigned: warm paper and green palette matching vibelink.co.ke, plain wording, real screens and a phone number instead of the terminal mock-up and tile grid.
vibelink.tech home page: added what it costs (pay by use or flat tier) with a calculator, the countries and payment methods supported, and common questions.
vibelink.tech home page redesigned in a bright blue style with feature cards, pricing and a cost calculator, supported countries, questions and a closing call to action.

Map: a tower can hold several PMP sector radios (each with a direction, beam width and reach drawn as a coverage slice), an unmanaged switch and a router, fanned out around it and linked with ethernet cables.
Map: customers are shown as a square (fibre), circle (PMP) or diamond (P2P); filter by connection type, and set a customer's connection and serving radio on their client page.

Direct settlement: an ISP with no Safaricom app of its own can have customers prompted under the platform name while the money goes straight to its own till, paybill or bank account (pick the bank, enter the account). Works for hotspot and PPPoE; nothing passes through the platform.

Payment gateways tidied: M-Pesa Paybill, Direct settlement, Flutterwave, Paystack, AzamPay and Yo! now sit in one "Payment method" dropdown (KopoKopo keeps its own card); Bank STK push and Till/paybill without API are no longer offered.
Site payment profiles can point a site at a Direct settlement gateway, so that site's hotspot and PPPoE payments go to its own till, paybill or bank account.
Payment gateways: "Direct settlement" is now called "Till / Bank", and KopoKopo moved into the same payment-method dropdown.
Customers: new Fibre, Wireless and Type not set tabs, and a bulk "Set connection…" for ticked clients (fibre, wireless PMP or P2P).

Site payment profiles can now be set for fibre or wireless customers only, so fibre income and wireless income go to different paybills (per site). Each profile has its own account prefix: reminders, the customer portal and the client page show it, and payments typed with it are matched automatically.
Fibre / PMP / P2P is now set per service (in a service's Edit, or when adding a service), not per customer, so one account can have a fibre line and a wireless one.

Wireless gets its own internet pool per router. Device-management pools hold the management addresses of customers' radios and fibre ONUs: reachable from the system, with no internet. Each service can be given a device address (radio or ONU); the router rule that blocks internet for the range is applied on Configure.
Menu tidied: Payments, Site payment profiles and Expenses are now tabs of one Payments page; Field app and Field team are one Field entry (the team page opens the app); Schedule moved under Support.

Map ↔ SkyPlan: "Export to SkyPlan" saves your towers, the radios/switches on them, fibre nodes and cables and customers (with their device address to monitor) as a SkyPlan project file; "Import from SkyPlan" brings a SkyPlan design's sites, equipment and fibre onto the map, updating what is already there instead of duplicating it.

Map: SkyPlan is no longer inside the Map page; it is hosted on its own (skyplan address) and the Map is the classic map again. Export to / Import from SkyPlan on the Map still move the network between them.
Licences: a licence date you set or extend by hand now holds until that date. The unpaid-statement lock used to put it back to yesterday on its next run, which is why manual extensions kept expiring.

Import from a router now also reads its saved hotspot users (not only who is online). By default each comes across as a voucher on the bundle named like its profile, with the time of that profile (or the user's own limit) less what it has used, the same name and password, and the phone number written in its comment. Permanent access codes are an option, with a tick-list. For PPPoE clients being brought in, three options (on by default): a new address from the billing pool (online ones are dropped to reconnect on it), a MAC lock to the device each is on, and its package from its profile.

Fixed PPPoE clients logging in and being dropped ("0.0.0.0") when their address pool was set to fibre or wireless only and they had no connection type: a pool made for another type is now used as a fallback instead of giving them no address.
Fixed imported hotspot users being refused at login: an imported voucher now takes its own code as its password (the login page sends only the code), not the password the router had.
Fixed router Configure stopping at the DNS proxy step with "done is not defined" when the guest DNS firewall rules were in the wrong order; the order is now repaired and reported.

Fixed hotspot vouchers whose clock never started (so they never expired): the 30-second online sync now starts the clock of any voucher it sees online, instead of relying only on FreeRADIUS reporting the login.

A new hotspot plan now creates its router profile on every hotspot router straight away. Before, codes of a brand-new plan (or a new device count) were accepted at login and then refused by the router until the next Configure.
Hotspot → Portal design: choose where the voucher-code box sits on the login page, above the bundles (as before) or at the bottom (the M-Pesa find-my-code box then shows at the top).
Live support now fits a phone: the chat opens above the queue, the reply box and Send button use the full width, and quick replies show in full.

Settings → API keys: make a key so SkyPlan can load your live network (towers, equipment, fibre, customers on the map) and, with a write key, save its design back. Keys are shown once and can be revoked.
Hotspot: a visitor whose phone sleeps or steps out of range for a few minutes is no longer logged out after 2 minutes (keepalive is now 10 minutes). Configure the router to apply it.
Hotspot: a returning visitor's phone is now logged back in by its MAC address (the router sent an empty password before, so it never worked). Configure the router to apply it.

Hotspot → Access codes: lock a code to its devices. The first devices that log in with it (up to Max devices) are remembered by MAC address and no other device can use it; forget a device to free its place.

Hotspot → Bundles: a bundle can be marked TV / console. Those are kept off the normal price list and shown under Add TV / console (own price and speed). A generated TV voucher can be activated on a TV or console from that page.

Access codes can now be used on a TV or console: on the Add TV / console page enter the code and its password, pick the device, and it is added to that code (counted in Max devices, removable under Hotspot → Access codes → Edit).

Router logs: the red "Radius request for unknown ip 10.250.x.x" lines are gone — PPPoE changes no longer carry an address that makes the hotspot look for a guest. A voucher bought or activated for a TV on the Add TV / console page now works only on that TV.

Router logs: no more red "Radius with no ip provided" / "unknown ip" lines — changes for a customer who is not online on the router are no longer sent to it; they apply when the customer next connects.
Hotspot Configure now keeps only the red RADIUS error lines ("Radius with no ip provided", "unknown ip") out of the router log; other hotspot messages, including failed guest logins, still show.
Router logs: the server now sets every router's log rules itself (shortly after the app starts, then hourly), so the red RADIUS error lines disappear on all routers without a Configure.

Security: the database port is no longer published to the internet, security headers and request limits on every site, a flood limit and tighter limits on sign-up and live chat, slow-connection timeouts, and updated libraries that fix reported vulnerabilities (including a mail-library flaw that could expose one ISP's SMTP login to another).
Ready to sit behind Cloudflare: the real visitor address is read through it, so sign-in and payment limits stay per person.
Hotspot login and Add TV / console pages are more compact on phones: smaller text and tighter spacing, so more fits on the screen without scrolling.
Hotspot: guests now keep their network address for 4 hours instead of 1, so a phone that sleeps for a while is no longer logged out for 'lost dhcp lease'. Configure the router to apply it.

Fixes guests being refused a correct code, or not connected automatically after paying, at busy times: the login server was running out of database connections. It now has more (10 to 48), and routers report usage every 60 seconds for hotspot and 2 minutes for PPPoE instead of every 10 and 30 seconds, which removes most of that load. Routers pick the new interval up within about 10 minutes.
Hotspot login: if a guest types an M-Pesa receipt code into the voucher box, their voucher is looked up and used; if they type a phone number, the page says so instead of a bare error.

Hotspot login: one box for a voucher code, an M-Pesa code or the phone number that paid. A phone number is sent a 6-digit code by SMS and signs the guest in; an M-Pesa code finds the voucher. The separate M-Pesa and phone links are gone.

Hotspot: a guest's device is now recorded on their voucher while they are online (and from their last session if they have already left), so a phone that drops or comes back from a walk is signed straight back in without retyping the code.

Hotspot: a guest with a running voucher is never disconnected for being idle. A phone that does not answer for 5 minutes is taken off the router's list and signed straight back in by its device when it returns. Applied to every router automatically within the hour.

SkyPlan is the Map again: the Map page opens SkyPlan loaded with the live network and customers, and new installations, customers and equipment appear in it by themselves (a quiet refresh every two minutes and whenever something new arrives). Edits are saved back. The classic map, with live online/offline colours, is one tab away.

SkyPlan (skyplan.vibelink.co.ke), once connected to billing, now stays current by itself: a customer added or moved in billing appears within two minutes, without pressing Load. Unsaved design work is never overwritten. The saved billing connection is now kept per user.

Hotspot login page: if the phone is signed in by its device while the page is still open (for example after the phone rejoined the Wi-Fi), the page now changes to 'You are connected' by itself instead of still showing the price list.

Hotspot: a phone that rejoined the Wi-Fi on a new address no longer gets refused as 'already logged in' by its own old session; the old one is cleared just before the new login. The login box also picks the M-Pesa code out of a whole pasted M-Pesa message.
Hotspot login: the 'Have a username and password instead?' link now works on its own, even if another part of the page fails to run on a customer's phone.

Hotspot: paying now signs the phone in by itself. The login page sends the phone's device with a purchase, and the paid voucher is tied to it, so the router connects it without the guest typing a code or keeping the page open while they are in the M-Pesa app.

Hotspot: the list of sites a guest may reach before signing in is now kept up to date by the server every hour, so it follows the site's addresses (including when they sit behind Cloudflare). This fixes the login page sometimes failing to reach the server.

Hotspot: a voucher code sent without its password (by an older login page, or a browser that submitted the form itself) is now accepted, since a voucher's password is its code. Fixes guests tapping Connect with a correct code and nothing happening.
Access codes: when a username is refused as "already used", it now says who has it (a voucher, a customer or another access code), and a name only left over from something deleted can be used again.

Routers → ⋯ → "Remove old local copies": removes the router's own hotspot users and PPP logins that billing already holds, so they no longer override billing. It previews first, skips anyone online right now and never touches a login billing does not hold. Offered after an import too.

Hotspot login: back to a plain Voucher code box, with the separate options for an M-Pesa code and for the phone number that paid. Typing an M-Pesa code or a phone number into the voucher box still points the guest the right way.

Hotspot → Access codes → Lock to devices: one button locks every access code to its devices, one turns the lock off for all, and one deletes all saved devices so each code starts learning its devices again.
Hotspot login: the 'Have a username and password instead?' link is smaller and now sits directly under the M-Pesa code option (and under the M-Pesa box when the voucher box is at the bottom).
Hotspot login: a button "I already have an active bundle: connect me" finds the running voucher of the phone and signs it in with one tap.
Payments: a hotspot payment is never held up by the 'which phone paid' lookup. It now runs on its own connection, so a missing table or an error there cannot stop the voucher being issued.
Payments → Reconcile statement: also takes a plain list of "CODE amount phone", never applies a code that is already on file under any channel, and lists what happened to each line.

SMS: a code text sent through the shared SMS relay is retried (up to three tries) when the relay answers 502 or times out, so a customer who just paid is no longer left without their code by a passing glitch.

Security: reconnecting a phone that already has a running bundle no longer reveals the voucher code. The server asks the router to sign that device in itself, so naming someone else's device address can no longer get you their code.
Hotspot login: the M-Pesa code box is smaller and no longer has the instruction line above it.

PPPoE: the router now waits 60 seconds (was 10) for a customer's line to answer before dropping the session, so a short stall no longer costs them a re-dial and a few seconds without internet. Applied to every PPPoE router within the hour.

title: Hotspot auto sign-in, router fixes, expenses calendar, access-code devices and field photos
items: Router refresh no longer rewrites firewall and NAT rules that are already correct: rules whose comment holds a dash or other special character were never recognised as unchanged and were pushed again every time.
Routers → Login pages: shows which hotspot routers still serve an old login page (read from the router itself) and updates the ones that are behind in one click.
Expenses: a Calendar tab to see and record each day's spending, and a month-by-month grid under Monthly bills to mark which months of each bill are paid, including earlier months.
Monthly bills: a bill can be paid to a shop or person who is not a supplier, and can be marked as paid in hotspot vouchers instead of money.
Hotspot: a purchase made on the hosted login page now remembers the buyer's phone (the router's page passes it along), so the paid voucher signs that phone back in by itself after it goes quiet.

Router Configure: a setting the router reports as true/false but we write as yes/no was never recognised as already correct, so the hotspot server, firewall and similar rules were re-written on every Configure (and refused on some routers). They are now skipped when already right.
Router Configure no longer fails with 'hotspot on that interface is already enabled': a hotspot server already on the managed bridge is adopted instead of trying to move another one onto it.

Access codes: a device that signs in with a code is remembered (up to the code's Max devices, TVs included) and signs itself back in next time without typing the code. Switching the code off, deleting it, clearing its devices or locking it to devices removes them.
Hotspot login: a wrong code now stays on screen in a box until it is tapped away (the page used to jump to another copy and wipe the message), and payment problems stay up for 12 seconds.

Access codes: devices online with a code are now picked up from what the router lists as connected (every 30 seconds), so remembering them no longer depends on a call from FreeRADIUS that was not always arriving.
Field app: a technician can delete a photo (for example a blurred one) while the job is open, and can add a screenshot from the phone's gallery to a job.
Leads: a lead that still shows as New moves to Contacted by itself as soon as someone adds a note to it or sets a follow-up date, so contacted leads no longer look new.

title: Find which code a device belongs to
items: Hotspot dashboard: a Find a device box. Paste a device address from the router's active list (a phone signed in by itself shows as its address there), a phone number or a code, and see which voucher or access code it belongs to, with the customer's phone, plan and expiry.

Hotspot dashboard → Live sessions now lists everyone connected on the router with the code behind each device address (phones the system signed in by themselves included), with a search box for finding one among many.

Leads: each lead that has a location now shows whether it can be served (can serve, marginal, weak signal or no coverage), worked out by SkyPlan from the terrain and your access points, with the sector, distance and expected speed. Open the Map once and it checks every lead.

Map (SkyPlan): customers now show how they are doing, with a ring: red when offline, amber when their line keeps dropping (3 or more drops in a day) or is connected but passing no traffic, grey when not paid. A small panel counts each group and filters the map to it.

Field app: when closing an install the technician can enter the signal the customer's radio shows (optional). On the Map, SkyPlan compares those readings with what it predicted for the same customers, shows how far off it is, and one click adds the difference as a correction for every customer and lead from then on.
Map (SkyPlan): customers, leads and their health are brought in from billing every time, also when you have unsaved design changes, and a customer placed or moved on the map shows up within seconds.

Clients: a Router / area filter shows only the customers of one MikroTik (for example Kabarnet) with a count per router, a Group by router option keeps each router's customers together, and each customer's router is shown under their name. The router name now also works in the search and the export.

Map (SkyPlan): click a customer or lead to move them to the right spot, set a customer's access point, or record progress on a lead (mark contacted, add a note, set a follow-up date). It is saved straight into billing with your own permissions. Customers and leads without a place are listed so you can place them by clicking the map.

Settings → Templates → When to remind customers: choose which days before a line expires the reminder text goes out, any of 7, 3 and 1 days. Until you choose, nothing changes (a text every day in the last 3 days).

Payments: a payment for a customer who has no package set is no longer lost. It goes to their balance. And if any payment fails to apply for another reason, it is now kept as an unmatched payment (with the reason) for a person to apply, instead of disappearing.
Payments → Reconcile statement: a pasted M-Pesa message now reads the account correctly (it used to take the date along with it, such as '21318 on 15', so the payment could not be matched).

Map (SkyPlan): wireless links and sectors drawn in SkyPlan are now saved into billing and shown on its Map (a wireless link between the two towers, an access point with its direction, beam and reach), and the whole design comes back as drawn on any computer that connects to billing.

title: Security settings
items: Settings → Security: anti-tunnel protection for hotspot routers (DNS and ping tunnels, IPv6, website-name check, VPN ports), and closing a router's API, Winbox and SSH to the tunnel and your own addresses with an automatic safety undo

New Shared links page: group the customers behind one radio, switch or ONU, and see at a glance whether a fault is the shared device's or one customer's, including unmanaged switches that are judged from the customers behind them
SkyPlan map: shared links panel showing each radio, switch or ONU with its health; tap one to see only its customers and a line from each
SkyPlan: make and edit shared links from the map: add a switch, radio or ONU (managed or unmanaged), then click customers to put them on it

Shared links can be fed from one another (receiving radio → switch → more radios), sit on a building or mast on the SkyPlan map, and a fault shows at the highest device that has it; customers can be searched on the map
Shared links: radios are now Access point or Station, and a radio already on the SkyPlan map can be picked as what feeds a switch or another radio

Things deleted in billing no longer come back from SkyPlan, and things deleted in SkyPlan can be removed from billing (it asks first); shared links also count customers assigned to the access point at their site

Shared links: radios, switches and ONUs get an address, model and frequency, are pinged every 2 minutes from the router they are locked to, and show Down when they stop answering; they are listed in SkyPlan's Network tab and their customers are evaluated automatically

Shared links: customers are put on a switch, station or fibre ONU only (a customer with their own dish stays on their access point), and customers are evaluated automatically unless their device is failing its ping

Client edit: 'Served by radio' now lists every radio on the map (access points, point-to-point radios and stations), and there is a new 'Connects through' choice for a customer who shares a switch, station or ONU

title: Router chaining monitor
items: Hotspot → Router chaining: routers plugged into a hotspot router's ports to extend the signal (Tenda and the like) are found by their MAC automatically and watched; two misses in a row mark one down, and you get one message however many went down together
Router chaining now scans only the LAN side (the hotspot's own bridge) and skips the uplink and WAN ports; anything an earlier scan wrongly picked up on an uplink port is removed
Router chaining: Scan now shows what it saw on each port and why it picked or skipped it, and finds a router that has only phones behind it even when it has no name or lease

Router chaining adds only devices that identify themselves as routers (by name or DHCP signature), never customers' phones or laptops; other devices on a port are listed in the scan with an Add as router button

Router chaining recognises a router by its maker's MAC prefix (Tenda today) and treats the addresses of one router's interfaces, a few apart, as the same router, so a label MAC still matches the one the bridge sees

Router chaining also finds and watches fibre units (ONU/ONT of xPON, GPON and EPON networks) plugged into hotspot ports, by their model name or maker's MAC, with a Type column, Routers and ONUs filters, and Add as ONU

Router chaining now knows the MAC prefixes of 1,599 router and gateway registrations (TP-Link, D-Link, Netgear, Ubiquiti, MikroTik, Sagemcom, Netis, Mercusys and many more) and 338 fibre-unit ones (FiberHome, V-SOL, Nokia, DZS, Calix…), built from the IEEE registry; cameras, plugs and phones that carry a router maker's prefix are not taken for routers

title: Router chaining monitor
items: Router chaining: a router counts as up while it is listed on the bridge (no more false 'down' for quiet extenders), each device shows why it is up or down, every router is scanned whatever its role, and a Routers table says what the last scan of each one did

Router chaining reads big routers faster (only the hotspot bridge, only the fields it needs), gives each router 60 seconds and reads three at a time, so one slow router can no longer stall the rest; a router that times out says so in the Routers table

Router chaining now finds xPON/GPON routers that send no name: a Huawei or ZTE device with no phone-like name is taken as an ONU, and model names with underscores or prefixes (HG8145V5, F670L, ZXHN, FiberHome HG6xxx, ZTE-ONT_1234) are recognised
Router chaining no longer reads a PPPoE router's thousands of session interfaces (only cable ports, bridges, VLANs and PPPoE clients), and a timeout now names the call it was waiting on

Router chaining scans big routers however long it takes: it runs in the background reading one cable port at a time (no more timeouts on a large hotspot), shows live progress in the Routers table, and keeps what each scan saw under What it saw

Router chaining never picks PPPoE customers' devices: MACs with an active PPP session or a locked MAC on a PPP secret are left out, ports where a PPPoE server runs are skipped, and any an earlier scan added are removed
